items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And Norman Granz, you know the impresario, went down and got him out

ctx.x: Well I don’t know. I don’t have too many, I don’t have too many gripes really. I’m kind of satisfied with the way I’ve done. Because see when I got my, after I got my, when I organized my band, I was the leader and I paid the salaries. You know for 21 years I was on the job, you know, one job. So I kind of made it up there. But Prez used to say, he would refer to people, they wasn’t no failure or anything but he acted like it. He referred, he says, “I don’t know,” he says, “all the ladies say they try to play…

making all the money.” He says, “I’m not making any money.” So and he says, “sometimes I don’t know if they’re playing like me or I’m playing like them.” You know he said kind of things like that, you know? So he really didn’t make too much money because he was you know everybody was trying to stay out of the Army and a lot of musicians beat it because it was a lot of jobs and things then, you know with everybody going in, and the musicians just wasn’t Army material, you know. So I remember one time we were out…

I want to ask you a question about jazz. You know we had talked, and you had talked about this too, how that in the early years of jazz of course before a certain time, like before Benny Goodman, all the bands were pretty much segregated, and then he began to hire Lionel Hampton and Teddy Wilson. But it seemed to me that the music was the one thing that allowed people to go back and forth without all these barriers, you know? Do you see a way that we can use music today to do the same things? Because it seems to…

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: So he found out that Norman GranZ was like giving him 500

ctx.x: You know, "Let's review the books." (Laughter.) So he says, "I haven't done so well, you know." I says, "What do you mean?" He says, "I never really made it on my own ." I said, "What do you mean, you haven't made it?" I says, "Man, you're a legend." I says, "You and Hawk." He says, "Yeah, but all the other ladies that they say play like me make all the money." So I says, "Well, I don't think you're a good businessman, I'll tell you that now." I says, "But you could have made it. I can even book you. All the…

So he found out that Norman GranZ was like giving him 500 and some of the others was getting 14 and Bean and them was getting 14. You see, to tell you about Prez, if you once do him a favor, he never stop paying you back. Everytime he'd think of something -- Flip told me he got nine cigarette lighters that Prez had given him, all cigarette --
